---
title: "Choose an example dataset"
description: "Synthetic data for fixed effects, instrumental variables, panels, and event studies."
sidebar: reference
---

These generators return synthetic data, not observations from the named
applications. Their reference pages describe arguments, column schemas, and
simulation assumptions. Pass `seed=` explicitly for reproducibility.

| Application | Generator | Useful variables and next step |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OLS, fixed effects, IV, and Poisson examples | [`pf.get_data()`](/reference/utils.utils.get_data.qmd) | `Y`, regressors `X1`/`X2`, fixed effects `f1`/`f2`, instruments, and weights; `model="Fepois"` supplies a Poisson outcome. Start with [OLS with fixed effects](/tutorials/ols-fixed-effects.qmd). |
| IVF instrument and motherhood penalties | [`pf.get_ivf_data()`](/reference/utils.dgps.get_ivf_data.qmd) | `earnings`, endogenous `num_children`, and the `ivf_success` instrument; see the [IV tutorial](/tutorials/instrumental-variables.qmd). |
| Bartik or shift-share applications | [`pf.get_bartik_data()`](/reference/utils.dgps.get_bartik_data.qmd) | A stylized synthetic instrument and local outcomes for the application; the generator does not construct an instrument from observed shares and shocks. |
| Encouragement design and treatment take-up | [`pf.get_encouragement_data()`](/reference/utils.dgps.get_encouragement_data.qmd) | Assignment, received treatment, outcome, and controls; population identities need not hold exactly in a finite sample. |
| Twin fixed effects and schooling | [`pf.get_twin_data()`](/reference/utils.dgps.get_twin_data.qmd) | Family identifiers, education, experience, and earnings; account for the controls used in the DGP when interpreting coefficients. |
| Worker panel with fixed effects | [`pf.get_worker_panel()`](/reference/utils.dgps.get_worker_panel.qmd) | Worker/time structure and covariates for within-worker comparisons. |
| Motherhood event study | [`pf.get_motherhood_event_study_data()`](/reference/utils.dgps.get_motherhood_event_study_data.qmd) | Unit, calendar period, treatment cohort, and event time. Never-treated units use `g=0` and `rel_year=-999`; see [difference in differences](/tutorials/difference-in-differences.qmd). |

```{python}
import pyfixest as pf

data = pf.get_data(N=100, seed=1234)
data.head()
```

Missing values and singleton groups can reduce a fitted model's sample.
Inspect `fit.sample_info` when comparing the input rows with estimation output.

See also [fitted results](/reference-guide/fitted-results.qmd) and the
[full function reference](/reference/index.qmd).
